一個聲部打第二拍、另一個打第一拍、第三個負責切分與填充。三層合起來就是森巴的「心: One part plays the second beat, another the first, and a third handles syncopation and filling. Together the three layers are samba's heartbeat
一支數十人的鼓隊走在森巴學校隊伍的前段，打同一個節奏，讓後面數百名舞者、以及跟著: A drum ensemble of several dozen players walks at the front of a samba school's line, playing one rhythm so that the hundreds of dancers behind and the whole street singing along step forward on the same beat. This is the bateria of Brazilian carnival. What it plays is not a piece but a time system on the move: the drums play as they walk, so the beat has to be solid enough that nobody has to stop to line up.
以濕布摩擦鼓內的竹棒、另一手按壓鼓皮改變張力，產生滑音，提供旋律性的線條與幽默感: Rub a stick inside the drum with a damp cloth while the other hand presses the head to change its tension, producing a glissando and giving the music a melodic line and a sense of humour
伴奏型是固定的、可預測的，所有人都在同樣的位置重複；呼叫型則故意打斷預期，長度短: Accompaniment patterns are fixed and predictable, everyone repeating at the same places; calls deliberately interrupt the expectation, short in length, sharp in outline, not blended into the texture. When the players hear a sound that does not belong to the cycle, they know to look up at the director. This design lets a whole ensemble work without watching a conductor, needing visual confirmation only when a signal comes.
停止與恢復，是整套系統的壓力測試。: Stopping and resuming is the stress test of the whole system.
先聽蘇爾多，找出那個前後搖晃的脈搏。抓住它，整首歌的骨架就出來了。: Listen to the surdo first and find that swaying pulse. Once you have it, the skeleton of the whole song is there.
再聽卡伊沙。它是判斷整隊整齊度最誠實的聲部。: Then listen to the caixa. It is the most honest part for judging how tight the ensemble is.
卡伊沙是時間的放大鏡。: The caixa is a magnifying glass on time.
同一套編制也用於學校的排練、廣場上的預演，以及部分非狂歡節的慶典。在這些場合，鼓: The same line-up is used for school rehearsals, for run-throughs in a square, and for some celebrations outside carnival. On these occasions the ensemble does not have to move, the difficulty of staying in sync drops, and the director allows more improvisation and longer solos.
和爵士大樂團相比，差別在譜與換曲的頻率。大樂團讀譜、分區塊、由指揮統一時值；巴特: Compared with a jazz big band, the difference is scores and how often the music changes. A big band reads, works in blocks, and has a conductor unifying the time values; a bateria reads nothing, a whole school polishes one theme song for a year, and the director's instructions are short calls and whistle blasts, not gestures.
和西非鼓樂隊相比，差別在編制的規模與分工方式。曼德鼓隊的敦敦鼓打出一個有名字的循: Compared with a West African drum ensemble, the difference is scale and how the work is divided. In a Mande ensemble the dunun play a cycle that has a name, and the leading djembe signals on top of that cycle; a bateria has no single owner of the cycle — the three surdo layers, the caixa and the tamborim each play their own place, sync rests on the density of the caixa and on the director's whistle, and the scale is far larger.
和馬拉卡圖相比，兩者都是巴西的遊行鼓隊，差別在誰控制段落。巴特利亞有總監，用雷皮: Compared with maracatu, both are Brazilian parade drum ensembles and the difference is who controls the sections. A bateria has a director who plays calls on the repinique and gives orders with a whistle, and the drum patterns follow the sections of the one theme song each samba school has that year; in maracatu the lead singer starts sections with a sung call, the group answers, the drums keep their own cycle patterns, the singing lies on top of the drum patterns and drives the changes, and the order of the procession and the royal roles are part of the rhythm as well. The first is the drum ensemble carrying the song; the second is the song carrying the drum ensemble.
它把拍子切成極細的等分，密度高到聽起來像一層噪音，但這層噪音其實是整隊的同步基準: It cuts the beat into extremely fine equal parts, dense enough to sound like a layer of noise, but that layer of noise is in fact the sync reference for the whole ensemble. As long as the caixas are together, the whole school is on the same time even if the surdos are tens of metres away and their sound has blurred into one; conversely, the easiest way to judge whether a school has rehearsed well is to hear whether the caixas sound like one person.
它是嚴格分層的：蘇爾多三層、卡伊沙一層、塔博林與金屬樂器各一層，每一層打的位置都: It is strictly layered: three surdo layers, one caixa layer, one each for the tamborim and the metal instruments, each layer playing a different place. Volume is a result, not a method.
巴特利亞就是一大群鼓手一起打同樣的節奏，越大聲越好。: A bateria is a big crowd of drummers all playing the same rhythm, and the louder the better.
巴特利亞的規模以數十人至上百人為常見，同一種樂器會有很多人一起演奏。這種「大量重: A bateria usually numbers from several dozen to over a hundred, with many people playing the same instrument together. This mass repetition is itself the design: one pattern played by a dozen people at once is thick enough to cover the noise of the crowd, and as long as half of them are still going the rhythm will not break.
找現場遊行的錄音或影片，注意鼓聲隨著隊伍移動時的都卜勒感與距離變化。: Look for a live parade recording or video, and notice the Doppler effect and the changing distance as the drum sound moves with the procession.
曲目上，巴特利亞依附的是「歌」而不是獨立的鼓曲。同一首主題歌會有固定的鼓型，鼓型: In repertoire, a bateria hangs on the song rather than on independent drum pieces. One theme song has fixed drum patterns, and the changes in those patterns follow the sections of the song: intro, verse, chorus and interlude each get their own treatment. So what the ensemble remembers is not a percussion piece but a map of one song's time.
最主要的場合是狂歡節的學校遊行。每所森巴學校在一年中準備一首主題歌，整所學校的服: The main occasion is the carnival school parade. Each samba school prepares one theme song a year, and the whole school's costumes, floats, dancers and drum ensemble are organised around it; in the parade the school passes down the parade avenue in order, with the bateria at the very front, behind the opening committee (comissão de frente) and the flag-bearer couple (casal de mestre-sala e porta-bandeira).
森巴學校的歌曲由領唱者（puxador）帶頭，整所學校答唱。巴特利亞必須留出空間: A samba school's song is led by the lead singer (puxador) with the whole school answering. The bateria has to leave room for the song to be heard, especially the first line. So when the song enters, the director thins out or temporarily drops some parts, lets the lead throw out the line, and then brings the ensemble back. This passage, where the drums give way to the voice, is the most important decision a bateria makes, and the easiest thing to miss in a recording.
森巴打擊樂隊（Bateria）— 森巴學校的遊行打擊隊，以蘇爾多鼓的分工撐起整所: Bateria — the parade percussion section of a samba school, whose division of work among the surdo drums holds up the whole school's singing and dancing. Ensembles and instrumentation by Next Door Sound Weavers.
森巴是兩拍的音樂，但巴特利亞從來不是「每個人打兩拍」。它把同一個兩拍循環拆成好幾: Samba is in two beats, but a bateria is never everyone playing two beats. It splits the same two-beat cycle into several layers, each interpreting the cycle differently.
森巴鼓隊的節奏是固定的，從頭到尾一樣。: The samba drum ensemble's rhythm is fixed, the same from beginning to end.
樂隊總監用雷皮尼克打出呼叫型：一種短、清楚、刻意跳出循環的樂句。呼叫有幾種功能—: The director plays calls on the repinique: a short, clear phrase deliberately breaking out of the cycle. Calls have several functions — starting the ensemble, stopping it after a certain phrase, bringing it back, or marking the sections of the song. The director usually uses a whistle at the same time: the whistle says when, the drum call says how. Two sets of signals are stacked because in the noise of a parade any single signal can be covered.
歌是另一個時間層。: Song is another layer of time.
注意哨聲與雷皮尼克的呼叫。那是整隊的神經系統，不是裝飾。: Notice the whistle and the repinique's calls. They are the ensemble's nervous system, not decoration.
為什麼是這些樂器？因為遊行需要三件事同時成立：一個不會散的低音、一個能填滿空間的: Why these instruments? Because a parade needs three things at once: a bass that will not come apart, a high frequency that fills the space, and a signal that can give orders on the spot. The surdo gives the bass, the caixa and tamborim give the high frequencies, the repinique and the whistle give the orders. The remaining instruments add decoration and polish.
由樂隊總監使用。打呼叫（chamada）來開始、轉段、停止或恢復: Used by the director. Plays calls (chamada) to start, change section, stop or resume
短促的哨音是段落進出的最高指令，比鼓更不容易被誤聽: The short whistle blast is the highest command for entering and leaving a section, and it is harder to mishear than a drum
移動時的同步，靠的是身體與位置。: Staying in sync while moving depends on the body and on position.
聽「鼓停下來、只剩歌」的段落，再聽它怎麼恢復。那是這個編制最難的地方。: Listen to a passage where the drums stop and only the song is left, then hear how it comes back. That is the hardest thing this line-up does.
蘇爾多的三層是整個系統的地基。兩個較大的蘇爾多打的拍點相反：一個在第二拍、一個在: The three surdo layers are the foundation of the whole system. The two larger surdos play opposite beats: one on the second beat, one on the first, alternating to make a swaying pulse. The smaller surdo inserts syncopation into that sway so the bass does not become too square. Only together are the three layers a complete samba feel; any one part heard alone sounds like an accompaniment with pieces missing. This also explains why surdo players carry the drum on their backs in a parade: the weight of the drum and the angle of the strap affect where the stick lands, but the relation between the three layers cannot change.
訊號與伴奏的分界，靠的是「會不會被預期」。: The boundary between signal and accompaniment is whether a sound can be expected.
連續不斷的細碎拍點，把兩拍的骨架填滿。它是整隊的織體，也是最容易聽出整齊度的聲部: An unbroken stream of small subdivisions filling in the two-beat skeleton. It is the ensemble's texture and the part in which tightness is easiest to hear
連續的高頻層，讓節奏在遠處也聽得見，並填滿鼓與鼓之間的空隙: A continuous high-frequency layer that lets the rhythm be heard at a distance and fills the gaps between drums
遊行中有一種段落，整隊會在訊號後同時停止，只剩歌聲或幾個聲部，然後在另一個訊號後: There is a passage in the parade where the whole ensemble stops together after a signal, leaving only the singing or a few parts, then comes back together after another signal. The stop is brief, but the moment of return has to be perfectly together; that rests not on memory from rehearsal but on the internal beat everyone holds in common. The first beat after the return is set by the surdo, and the ensemble comes in again on the same beat.
遊行隊伍往前走，鼓手背著鼓、看著前方，視線被樂器與人群擋住。所以同步不能依賴看。: The parade moves forward, the drummers carry their drums and look ahead, and their view is blocked by instruments and people. So sync cannot depend on sight. The surdo players rely on the rhythm of their own steps and the overall field of bass sound; the caixa players rely on hearing the players around them; the ensemble relies on the director's whistle and the repinique's calls. Position matters too: players of the same instrument usually stand together, so that the sound forms a block that can correct itself rather than scattering.
雷皮尼克是指揮，但它不在前面揮手。: The repinique is the conductor, but it does not stand in front waving.
高、短、乾的敲擊，打出與歌咬合的切分型，是森巴最辨識的聲音之一: A high, short, dry stroke that plays the syncopated pattern interlocking with the song; one of samba's most recognisable sounds
鼓型跟著歌的段落變化，而且總監會用呼叫與哨子即時改變長度、密度與進出。同一個節奏: The drum patterns change with the sections of the song, and the director changes their length, density and entries on the spot with calls and the whistle. The same rhythm is adjusted to the occasion during a parade.
鼓隊在遊行中只是伴奏，主角是舞者與花車。: The drum ensemble is only accompaniment in the parade; the dancers and floats are the stars.
鼓隊是整所學校的時間來源。歌的長度、舞群的動作、隊伍前進的速度，都掛在同一個拍子: The drum ensemble is the source of time for the whole school. The length of the song, the movements of the dancers and the speed of the procession all hang on the same beat; once the drums go wrong, the whole school goes wrong with them.
